story.trigger: Ostell Bank's questionnaire asks how production is separated from testing. Everything is in one account. Chen joins Callvale to lead security.
story.problem: Callvale runs development, testing and production in one AWS account. The bank requires an isolated production environment and audit logs that operators cannot change. No workload can run outside two approved Regions. The rules must apply to every account, including future accounts.
story.choice: AWS Control Tower with seven accounts in three organizational units, and service control policies.
story.question: How do I make sure that even a production administrator cannot turn off the audit log?
story.note: AWS RAM shares the transit gateway of chapter 11 with the workload accounts.

orchestrator_focus: Security block chapter; reader's weakest domain (Secure 45%).
Completeness of can-or-cannot facts: SCP/RCP scope (management account, root user, service-linked roles, outside principals), what policies grant, what member accounts can change.

Comparisons with neighbours: IAM policy vs SCP vs RCP vs permissions boundary vs declarative policy; Control Tower vs Organizations alone vs Config/Security Hub; RAM vs resource-based policy vs cross-account role.
Changes since mid-2022: SCP full IAM language, SCP quotas 10 / 10,240, RCPs, declarative policies, accounts per organization, Control Tower controls on RCPs and declarative policies, auto-enrollment.
Displays of number-free facts: at most 8 words copied verbatim from a quote.
